neighbours.label: The noun naming something absent after 'no'/'never ... any' (no symptoms, never any schooling, no children), vs the same noun when it is present
fire: Many of the infected birds showed no symptoms during the first week.
In the remote villages, most girls never got any schooling at all.
The elderly couple had no children and left their house to a charity.
Half of the workers surveyed had no insurance of any kind.
Some carriers of the virus never develop any symptoms.
Refugee children often go years without any schooling.
The widow had no relatives nearby to help with the farm.
The new recruits arrived with no experience in the field.
quiet: Many of the infected birds showed clear symptoms during the first week.
In the remote villages, most girls got three years of schooling.
The elderly couple had four children and left their house to them.
Half of the workers surveyed had private insurance through their union.
Some carriers of the virus soon develop severe symptoms.
Refugee children often receive free schooling in the camps.
The widow had many relatives nearby to help with the farm.
The new recruits arrived with years of experience in the field.

predictions: The absent noun reaches 0.25-0.6; the same noun with a positive quantifier stays under 0.12. 'no known function' and 'did not undergo any training' were weak in probes, so some fire items may miss.
short: noun of absence after no/never any
notes: Card: 'no offense', 'no predicted function', 'without actually touching', 'Abstain from sex', 'never receive any schooling', 'no symptoms', 'no children'. Probe: 'never receive any schooling' 0.502, 'had no symptoms' 0.372, 'mild symptoms' 0.114, 'no known function' 0.078, 'did not undergo any training' 0.006; positive controls 0.008-0.011.
